- Expired download links stop being a dead end. A link that dies mid-download
  (signed URLs that expire, host auth) now parks the task as "expired" with
  your bytes kept, instead of marking it failed - and every surface shows you
  the way back:
  - GUI: the row turns amber "expired" with a globe button that opens the
    new **Refresh address** dialog. Paste a fresh link and the dialog probes
    it first, showing exactly what the swap keeps ("keeps 5.4 GiB of 50 GiB")
    before anything changes; the task resumes by itself if it was running.
    Swapping to a different file version warns you instead of silently
    adopting it.
  - Browser extension: copy a fresh link anywhere and the capture chip offers
    **"Refresh keeps X of Y already on disk"** when the link matches one of
    your unfinished downloads - one tap swaps the address in and resumes.
    The daemon verifies each match through the same gate a real refresh
    runs, so the number on the button is real.
  - CLI: `ripdl refresh <id> <url> [--resume]`, and `ripdl ls` shows
    `stale(auth)` on parked tasks.
- `.ripdl.json` sidecar files next to partial downloads are hidden on
  Windows - no more files jumping around your Downloads folder in Explorer.
- Fixed: a browser extension newer than the app no longer stalls page offers
  against an older daemon (unknown commands now answer under the caller's
  own id instead of leaving the page waiting out a 15 s timeout).
